content.title: Access Arvada: ADA Transition Plan
content.summary: The City of Arvada is updating its ADA Transition Plan, originally established in 2020, to assess progress and address community needs for accessibility. Feedback from previous community engagements has been incorporated into the draft plan, which will be presented to the City Council and shared with the public later this year. The City remains committed to improving services and infrastructure to ensure inclusivity and compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act.
content.body:
## 2026 Update

The City is updating the ADA Transition Plan to continually assess progress and needs since the plan's inception in 2020.

The City has completed updates to our ADA Transition Plan and is seeking feedback on the draft of the plan. [Feedback from the 2025 engagement](https://PublicInput.com/Report/dqcjbdsqii4) has been incorporated into the plan updates.

Thank you to those who participated in the final review of the [**draft of Arvada's ADA Transition Plan**](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VIFGMmWubaxY6E96VmBWtn5sjS9Xl9NV/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=112559812600375277075&rtpof=true&sd=true). Feedback is being incorporated into the final plan which will be presented to City Council and shared with the community later this year.

## Overview

The City of Arvada is committed to ongoing efforts to improve the City's services, facilities and other infrastructure to ensure they are inclusive and accessible to everyone. The City maintains an Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Transition Plan to evaluate the City's progress in meeting the requirements of the ADA, and to identify and prioritize next steps. We are required by law and committed to making continual progress toward this goal.

## Program milestones

### Self-assessment

In 2020, the City performed a review of compliance with the ADA for City services and assets including, City buildings, parks, trails, transportation facilities, the City website, and other communications.

### Draft ADA Transition Plan

The City’s first ADA Transition Plan was developed in 2020 with an identified list of opportunities to improve accessibility and prioritize ongoing work.

### Community feedback

- In 2021, the community was asked for feedback on the draft plan to help prioritize work. [Watch a recording of the public meeting](https://youtu.be/_QPyhwwKe3c) held March 9, 2021 on YouTube.
- In 2025, community feedback will be solicited to inform updates to the plan and ensure the plan continues to reflect lived experiences and community priorities.

### Council presentation

The team presented the ADA Transition Plan to the City Council in 2021. In 2025, the team provided updates about the work and the upcoming updates to the plan.

- Watch the [presentation from April 12, 2021 (YouTube)](https://youtu.be/VD95ynXzYWc)
- Watch the [presentation from January 13, 2025 (YouTube)](https://youtu.be/oy4n2nYvi7M?si=GXnByctvur3IKlaA&t=4260)

### Implement and ongoing evaluation

The City team will continue to implement work identified through the ADA Transition Plan. Periodically, the plan is reviewed to assess progress and update the identified gaps, opportunities, and priorities.
